title: Corsankell: James and his sons
standfirst: Hugh’s large working branch now follows the preferred Corsankell–Kilwinning route. John-3193 is selected as uncertain father; the Mid Calder James is retained as an alternative. Exact generations and the later minister’s own identity remain unresolved.

status.label: Corsankell sons documented; Hugh link uncertain

question: How did the Corsankell household connect to William's Glasgow burgh family?
answer: The preferred local model places Hugh-1603 under John-3193 of Corsankell/Kilwinning, uncertain. This replaces the unsupported Mid Calder placement without changing dates or adding an invented generation. The 1571 NRS catalogue abstract names James elder's sons James and John, while the 1559–60 teind list places elder and younger James at Corsankell. It does not identify James elder's father, establish the city connection, or securely identify the named John with a later Kilwinning profile. The 16 October 2026 working reconstruction selects James younger as Glasgow-3178’s uncertain father, using Stevenston locality and generation; her records name no parent, and James elder, Edward and another family remain alternatives. No mother is assigned.

chapters.title: Hugh’s 137-profile branch: prefer the local Corsankell family
body: Prefer John Glasgow-3193 of the Corsankell/Kilwinning family as Hugh Glasgow-1603’s uncertain working father. This materializes the leading Ayrshire placement already argued in the maintained five-generation map. The 1571 Corsinkell deed expressly names John as James elder’s son; the earlier Kilwinning tenant appearances are attributed to him as probable. Hugh’s surviving profile account describes an Ayrshire progenitor, his son’s account is centred on Kilwinning, and the following households lie in Kilwinning, Ayr and Kilbirnie. These successive local settings favour the documented nearby family over the existing Mid Calder/Inveresk father attachment, which depends on an online tree and has no movement, household or property bridge. A John-to-Hugh-to-John sequence is compatible supporting context, not a naming rule. Father is selected as a revisable one-generation model, rather than leaving the previously preferred local route only in prose.

Hugh remains a tree-derived generation: no inspected contemporary record securely identifies him, names his father or establishes his own c.1600 birth. John’s before-1540 boundary means a birth for Hugh near 1600 would make him an older father, around 60 or more; a grandson or collateral position may fit better. Neither date is changed to fit. An earlier Hugh birth is possible but is not adopted as a new estimate, and no missing person is invented. The 1571 John is documented as a son, while his additional Kilwinning identity is only probable. John’s brother James Glasgow-3921, another local Glasgow family, an omitted generation and the former James Glasgow-991 placement remain alternatives. This is stronger locality reasoning, not a probable or proved father assessment. The 1677 deed-index Hugh, preacher of the gospel, remains an unresolved identity comparison and supplies no evidence for this father choice.

The existing 137-profile pre-1850 working child side is rerouted from James of Mid Calder to John of Corsankell; descendants retain every earlier identity and relationship qualification. No mother, spouse, merge, new person or changed vital field is selected. Hugh-to-John-1604 and the minister’s separate father and duplicate questions are unchanged. Shared Y-DNA can motivate the extended-family model but cannot identify this father. Both proposed fathers already belong to the same working component: cohort membership, working component and pair coverage, supported connectivity and confidently marked connectivity remain unchanged. This is a better-supported placement within the working tree, not a newly connected component or confidence upgrade. No new source inspection or live WikiTree save is claimed.

The earlier Murieston father-review impact was 216 profiles below James. Rerouting Hugh’s 137-profile branch leaves 79 below James in the current pre-1850 working model; these are dated profile-impact counts, not changes in population or proofs of descent.

chapters.title: Two Jameses at Corsankell
body: The teind material distinguishes James elder from James younger at the Stevenston holding.
The labels establish a local household setting but do not on their own say how the men were related.

chapters.title: The charter supplies the relationship
body: The 1571 charter explicitly calls James and John sons of James elder.

The record-defined John is represented by Glasgow-3193 after Glasgow-4061 was merged into it on 27 September 2026. His additional Kilwinning/Burrowland/Dalgarven event attributions remain probable; they are separate from the documented 1571 father-son role.
